systems.name: Clinic Booking
systems.goal: Patients book visits online, the front desk runs each clinician's day, and a reminder goes out the day before each visit.

modules.name: Front desk app
modules.does: Where staff see each clinician's day, book and move visits, and set hours.

modules.name: Booking page
modules.does: Where patients pick a free slot and book a visit.

modules.name: Web API
modules.does: Serves both apps over HTTP, finds the clinic from the subdomain, and turns each request into one module call.

modules.name: Booking
modules.does: Creates, moves, and cancels visits, rejects overlaps and times outside weekly hours, and keeps clinicians' hours.

modules.name: Patients
modules.does: Keeps patients' contact details, and finds a returning patient by phone or email.

versions.why: Clinics lose about one visit in ten to no-shows, and reminders were the first thing they asked for.

decisions.title: One service, one folder per module
decisions.why: It's the house rule, and two engineers can't run more. Modules talk only through interfaces, so one could become a service later. Not chosen: separate services.

decisions.title: Each module owns its store interface
decisions.why: src/db/ implements the stores with Prisma, so business logic never imports Prisma and tests use in-memory stores. Not chosen: one shared repository layer.

decisions.title: Double bookings are stopped twice
decisions.why: Booking checks for overlaps, and a database constraint catches two bookings made at the same moment. Not chosen: a lock per clinician.

decisions.title: Times are stored in UTC
decisions.why: Weekly hours stay in local time and are turned into UTC per day, so daylight saving doesn't shift anyone's hours. Not chosen: storing local times.

decisions.title: Booking announces events instead of calling Reminders
decisions.why: Booking stays the same when something new reacts to visits, like a waitlist. Not chosen: Booking calling Reminders directly.

decisions.title: Reminders run from a table, not a queue
decisions.why: About 6,000 reminders a day fit in one table checked every minute, and moving a visit is one row update. Not chosen: a queue like SQS, one more thing to run.

decisions.title: One channel per provider
decisions.why: Clinics have already asked about WhatsApp. Adding it means one new channel and no change to Reminders. Not chosen: calling Twilio and Postmark from Reminders.

decisions.title: Availability is its own module
decisions.why: Hours and time off change every week; booking rules rarely do. Booking only reads open hours. Not chosen: keeping hours inside Booking, as in v2.

openQuestions.title: Patients moving their own visits
openQuestions.detail: Today they call the front desk. Online needs a link in the reminder and a way for patients to prove who they are.

openQuestions.title: Reminder timing
openQuestions.detail: Assumed one reminder, 24 hours before. Some clinics may want 48 hours, or a second one on the morning of the visit.

openQuestions.title: Clinicians at two clinics
openQuestions.detail: Assumed each clinician works at one clinic. If not, Availability needs hours per clinic.
